# Composable infectious disease modelling

## Three outbreaks, the same problems

- **COVID-19, 2020.** $R_t$, the number of new infections per infected
  person, daily for thousands of locations
- **mpox, 2022.** Nowcasting for UKHSA. Nowcasting is estimating what
  has already happened but has not yet been reported
- **Ebola disease caused by Bundibugyo virus, Democratic Republic of
  the Congo (DRC), 2026.** One joint model across five data streams,
  refit on every push
- Each time the methods from the last outbreak were not reusable
- Each time the models did not fit the data sources that existed, and
  the data changed under us

![](../figures/exchange-timeline.png){width="72%" fig-align="center"
fig-alt="A timeline from 1760 to 2026 in two panels with an axis break.
Grey dots for Bernoulli 1760, Ross 1911, Kermack and McKendrick 1927,

## Analysing data and processes separately, or all together

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="42%"}
- The Office for National Statistics (ONS) COVID-19 Infection
  Survey. 4M+ swabs, 150K households, £500M+, April 2020 to March 2023
- External modellers accessed only summarised prevalence, not underlying
  observations
- Lison et al. found biases at each step. Joint modelling of all steps
  together avoided these cascading biases
- But models are difficult to develop within policy-relevant timelines

::: {.attribution}
Lison et al. (2024),
[doi:10.1371/journal.pcbi.1012021](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1012021)
:::
:::
::: {.column width="58%"}
![](../figures/exchange-composable-ons-cascade.jpg){width="94%"
fig-align="center"
fig-alt="Four panels of the survey chain fitted as one model: prevalence,
incidence, antibody prevalence and R_t, each with a posterior ribbon over
the survey period."}

::: {.attribution}
Abbott and Funk (2022),
[doi:10.1101/2022.03.29.22273101](https://doi.org/10.1101/2022.03.29.22273101)
:::
:::

## What we want from any approach

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- **Uncertainty and inference.** Joint and staged inference that avoids
  the cascading biases, and automatic differentiation for fitting
- **Model structure.** Components separated by process type, and models
  nested inside models
- **Workflow.** One specification that is useful for simulation and for
  inference

::: {.callout-warning}
These design considerations were developed by the authors and have not
yet received broader community input.
:::
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](../figures/exchange-composable-requirements.png){width="100%"
fig-alt="Table 1 of the paper. Twelve proposed requirements under six
themes, each paired with the problem that motivates it, from

::: {.attribution}

barriers to rigorous infectious disease modelling* ·
[epiaware.org/approaches](https://epiaware.org/approaches/)
:::
:::

## What is composable modelling?

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
Components can be reused across contexts and combined in different
configurations whilst maintaining statistical rigour.

Abbott et al., *Composable probabilistic models can lower barriers to
rigorous infectious disease modelling*
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](../figures/exchange-composable-structure.png){height="700px"
fig-align="center"
fig-alt="Four applications drawn as graphs over a band of shared parts.
The incubation period model appears in all four and the latent infection
model in three."}

::: {.attribution}
Figure 1 of Abbott et al., *Composable probabilistic models can lower
barriers to rigorous infectious disease modelling*, in CDC clearance
:::
:::

## [`ComposableTuringIDModels.jl`][ctim]

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="56%"}
```julia
using ComposableTuringIDModels, Distributions, Turing

# Renewal infections with an autoregressive log-R_t prior
renewal = Renewal(;
    generation_time = Gamma(1.4, 1 / 0.38),
    rt = AR(; ϵ_t = HierarchicalNormal(std = HalfNormal(0.1))),
    initialisation = Normal(log(1.0), 1.0))

# Observation layers: delay → ascertainment → negative-binomial noise
obs = LatentDelay(
    Ascertainment(
        NegativeBinomialError(),
        Intercept(Normal(log(0.4), 0.1))),
    truncated(Normal(5.0, 2.0), 0.0, Inf))

model = IDModel(renewal, obs)

# Fit to case data with Turing's NUTS
chain = sample(as_turing_model(model, cases, length(cases)),
    NUTS(0.95), MCMCThreads(), 100, 2)
```

::: {.attribution}
[epiaware.org/approaches/composable-turing-models](https://epiaware.org/approaches/composable-turing-models.html)
:::
:::
::: {.column width="44%"}
- A library of parts over [`Turing.jl`][lk-turingjl]
- Three kinds of part. An infection model, an observation model, and
  prior models nested in the slots of both
- Parts carry their own priors
- A model definition does not know about the data. One definition
  simulates and fits
- Adding a new application means defining only the new parts
:::
::::

## [`ComposedDistributions.jl`][cd]

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="56%"}
```julia
using ComposedDistributions, Distributions

# BDBV-inspired delay tree: parallel pathways
# with sequential, resolve, and compete nested together
tree = @uncertain compose((
    clinical = sequential(
        :onset_admit => Gamma(Normal(1.2, 0.2), 3.0),
        :admit_resolve => resolve(
            :death => (Gamma(2.0, 3.5), 0.3),
            :discharge => (Gamma(1.0, 8.0), 0.7))),
    surveillance = sequential(
        :onset_notif => Gamma(0.7, 20.0),
        :notif_compete => compete(
            :confirmed => Gamma(2.0, 1.0),
            :lost => Gamma(5.0, 0.5))),
))

# Draw a synthetic case, or evaluate a real one's likelihood
case = rand(tree)
logpdf(tree, case)
```

::: {.attribution}
[epiaware.org/approaches/composed-distributions](https://epiaware.org/approaches/composed-distributions.html)
:::
:::
::: {.column width="44%"}
- Write the epidemiology as [`Distributions.jl`][lk-distributionsjl]
  distributions. The probabilistic programming language becomes optional
- A case's event history is a tree. `sequential` chains delays,
  `resolve` picks an outcome with a probability, `compete` races two
- The whole tree is itself a distribution. It slots in wherever a delay
  is needed inside a larger model
- Parameter uncertainty is an ordinary leaf
:::
::::

## Real-time nowcasting (`EpiNow2`)

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- Reuses the autoregressive prior from the paper's first case study,
  swapping the Poisson observation model for a negative binomial one
- `broadcast_weekly` wraps it to give piecewise constant weekly $R_t$
  values
- `ascertainment_dayofweek` adds day-of-week reporting effects
- Two `LatentDelay` wrappers compose the incubation and reporting
  delays by nesting structs

::: {.callout-important}
No new components needed and took ~ 3 hours
:::

::: {.attribution}
One configuration of `EpiNow2` replicated, not a benchmark. Abbott et
al. (2020),
[doi:10.12688/wellcomeopenres.16006.2](https://doi.org/10.12688/wellcomeopenres.16006.2)
:::
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](../figures/exchange-composable-epinow2-results.png){height="820px"
